notes: The only row where the seller is a company that appears in a state register under the exact name it trades as, and that is worth more than the price difference. AXIVORA CONNECT LTD, company 16780591, status Active, incorporated 13 October 2025, SIC codes for wired telecommunications and for data processing and hosting. A buyer checking the wrong one would conclude the wrong thing. The price is the soft field. The group page says EUR 1.25 per quarter for this plan and per month for the larger one; the product page prints EUR 1.25 with no cycle. Read as quarterly, it is EUR 0.4167 a month or USD 0.4664; read as monthly it is USD 1.3991, which is still under the line. Both readings clear the USD 1.50 bar, so the verdict does not turn on it, and the arithmetic records both. The real constraint is the product: a single /128 and no IPv4 at all, which the vendor states as 'you cannot access any IPv4 internet'. That makes it a WireGuard endpoint, an IPv6 web origin, or a BGP experiment, and not a general-purpose box. What is not established: the payment rails and whether a card is required at checkout; the actual billing cycle; and whether the fair-use bandwidth has any real ceiling. The 1 GB sibling MCI-N-B is out of stock, so the 384 MiB plan is the only one buyable today.

extras.price_arithmetic: Two readings, both recorded. As quarterly: EUR 1.25 / 3 = EUR 0.4167 a month, / 0.89342 EUR per USD = USD 0.4664 a month, and EUR 1.25 = USD 1.3991 out of pocket every quarter. As monthly: EUR 1.25 / 0.89342 = USD 1.3991 a month. The group page states 'per quarter' for MCI-N-C and 'per month' for MCI-N-B, which is the reading used for the headline figure.
